Finite verification is supporting only; the proof covers all n≥4.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source defines precisely the uniform-floor discounted hitting invariant and develops path-gap transfers plus spider algorithms, but does not derive the wheel maximin balancing theorem or a formula resolving the coupled hub contribution for every discount and threshold. A closely related 2024 group-hitting-probability paper optimizes evaluation and ranking queries with one starting vertex, not minimum-cardinality target selection subject to worst-vertex coverage. The 2013 random-walk domination article uses fixed-budget aggregate finite-horizon objectives. The closest found published graph-class result treats complete bipartite graphs, not these wheels, so it has no evident reduction to the balance theorem. Residual risk remains for unindexed equivalent pinned-consensus or facility-location formulations; searches do not establish priority by themselves.
residual_risks: Equivalent wheel source-placement results could occur in alternative terms, especially penalized hitting probability, facility location, or pinned consensus; comprehensive bibliographic priority is not certified.

value.rationale: This is an exact infinite-class formula for a new graph-placement invariant rather than a substitution into a generic transfer: all rim gaps couple through one global hub equation, yet strict convexity yields a shared optimum in both hub regimes and O(n) exact arithmetic computation. The explicit W4 rational-parameter witness shows even an unusually well-connected hub may be absent from every cardinality-optimal source set. This addresses worst-vertex robustness, not merely finite values or a routine exercise; no unsupported application claims are required.
